messages:
Alex: Quick heads-up — canary for model-x shows p95/p99 spike after the recent kernel-selector tweak. putting the raw profile here.
Maria: ok what changed in selector logic?
Alex: we now bias to the multihead kernel when microbatch >= 13. scheduler also sometimes splits prefill into two microbatches which triggers a kernel swap mid-request.
Todd: do you have numbers / flamegraph snippet?
Alex: pasted small excerpt:
```
profile summary:
  prefill: 18.1ms
  decode: 9.3ms/token
  kernel-switch overhead: ~9.8ms (cold switch)
  kv-cache hit: 60% (baseline 94%)
```
Maria: kv-hit drop explains a lot. were KV warmups affected by the split?
Alex: yeah — split moves the prefill into a later worker that hasn't warmed KV, so we pay cold loads + kernel swap.
Priya: the canary also doubled max-microbatch from 16->32 to chase throughput — could be interacting badly.
Todd: so classic SLO vs throughput tradeoff: bigger microbatches win unit-cost but increase chance of cross-worker kernel decisions and KV coldness -> tail.
Maria: mitigation ideas?
Todd: 1) clamp microbatch for short sequences (e.g. `--max-microbatch=12`) 2) add async KV prefetch on prefill handoff 3) prefer fastpath kernel for seq_len < 128 to avoid swap.
Priya: I ran a tiny canary with `--max-microbatch=12` + `kv_prefetch=async` on 3 hosts: p95 42ms -> 33ms, p99 120ms -> 102ms. throughput down ~6%.
Maria: 6% throughput drop seems acceptable given tail improvement and SLOs.
Alex: agreed. we should aim for a scheduler heuristic that predicts post-split kernel decision and avoids splits that force a swap if it would increase p99 > threshold.
Todd: I'll prototype a simple estimator: compute expected microbatch sizes after routing, if kernel_choice(before) != kernel_choice(after) and delta_p99_est > 10% then prefer same-worker routing or smaller initial batches.
Priya: I'll run a broader perf sweep across seq bins and different model sizes. want to capture regressions on long-context workloads too.
infra-bot: canary group deployed with the `--max-microbatch=12` experiment to 3 hosts in us-west.
perf-bot: noted. baseline vs experiment metrics collected, I'll post a dashboard link shortly.
Maria: also add a KV warmup burn-in on worker handoff (hit-rate target 90% before accepting live traffic for that shard).
Alex: sounds good. I'll open a PR for the scheduler heuristic with a runtime flag and telemetry for "kernel_switch_count" and "kv_cold_loads".
Todd: assigned to me to prototype scheduler change. ETA EOD tomorrow for a first pass.
Priya: i'll run the full suite after Todd's change, then we can A/B for 24h.
Alex: thanks. short checklist: Todd prototype scheduler heuristic; Priya perf sweep; Maria add KV warmup gating; Alex PR + telemetry. :thumbsup:
Maria: also adding a quick note to the runbook about how kernel-selection + microbatch sizing interacts with KV warming.
Alex: perfect — closing the loop here. :)
